input: Teamwork is useful because people have different skills.
question: Why is teamwork useful?

key_issues.message: “people have different skills”语法正确但偏平实，用“bring different skills to the table”更自然、更地道。
回答直接切题，但只给了一个理由，没有进一步说明不同技能为什么让团队合作有用。

feedback.optimization_summary: 保留原句核心意思和单句结构，只把“have different skills”升级为更地道的“bring different skills to the table”。没有添加用户未提供的新理由或例子。
feedback.final_upgraded_answer: Teamwork is useful because people bring different skills to the table.
feedback.reference_answer: Teamwork is useful, but I'd say its real value shows up when a problem is too messy for one person to even define properly. If you're stuck on your own, you can go round in circles for hours without noticing you're asking the wrong question. In a team, someone usually says something that makes you stop and rethink. That's not about splitting tasks or covering weaknesses — it's about the thinking itself getting sharper because other people poke holes in it. Of course, this only works if people actually speak up. If everyone just agrees with the loudest voice, a team can be slower and more confident than one person, which is a bad combination. So teamwork is useful mainly when it forces you to test your own assumptions.
feedback.reference_angle_summary: 独立主线：团队合作的价值在于通过他人质疑来修正和深化个人思考，而非分工或互补短板；示例不代表用户经历。
feedback.content_diagnosis: 原回答直接回答问题，主线明确：团队合作有用，因为人们技能不同。相关性高，没有跑题或重复，但展开不足，只停留在“不同技能”这一层，没有说明这种差异如何产生价值。
feedback.structure_diagnosis: 原回答是单一因果句，逻辑连接清楚，但信息量较少，没有分层或补充说明。
feedback.optimization_advice: 如果想冲更高分，可以补充一句说明不同技能如何互补，例如有人擅长规划、有人擅长执行，但不要编造具体经历。也可以加一个简短例子，但必须是你真实想到或经历过的内容。

feedback.reference_answer: Teamwork is useful mainly because it lets people cover each other's weak spots. Nobody is good at everything, so when you work with others, you can lean on their strengths and they can lean on yours. I remember doing a group project where I was fine with research but terrible at presenting. One of my teammates was the opposite, and honestly, the final result was way better than anything I could have done alone. It also speeds things up, because you can split tasks and get feedback early instead of going down the wrong path. And on top of that, working in a team teaches you how to deal with different personalities, which is a skill you need pretty much everywhere. So it's not just about getting the job done faster — it's also about learning from each other along the way.
feedback.reference_angle_summary: 独立主线：团队合作的价值在于互补短板、加速反馈并锻炼人际协作；示例为虚构，不代表用户经历。

takeaway_expressions.why_useful: 高频且可迁移，用于解释合作、友谊、家庭等话题时非常自然。
takeaway_expressions.example: In a good team, people cover each other's weak spots instead of blaming each other.
takeaway_expressions.usage_note: weak spots 比 weaknesses 更口语化，适合日常对话。

takeaway_expressions.why_useful: 比 use their advantages 更地道，适合讨论团队、领导力、学习等话题。
takeaway_expressions.example: A smart manager knows how to lean on each person's strengths.
takeaway_expressions.usage_note: lean on 本意是“靠在……上”，引申为依靠，语气自然。

takeaway_expressions.why_useful: 适用于工作、学习、项目等场景，能具体说明效率提升的原因。
takeaway_expressions.example: We share drafts in the group chat so we can get feedback early.
takeaway_expressions.usage_note: early 放在动词后，表示“及早”，比 in the early stage 更简洁。
